messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: spike in 504/gateway timeouts for private-peering-prod (region: eu-west-1). Auto-paging on-call. Severity: P1

jordana: acknowledged, I'm oncall. digging in now. @liam @maya FYI

liam: grabbing logs and metrics. which customers are affected? any external-facing endpoints?

sarah-cs: several customers filing errors — noticed from support tickets: tenant-42, tenant-88, and one internal smoke-runner. errors look like gateway 504s from our private inference gateway.

maya: looking at peering telemetry — I see a large number of stale route withdrawals for the peering attachment to customer-vpc-7. BGP flaps starting ~1719821000. Could be route propagation issue.

jordana: can you confirm which path the requests take? ingress -> peering -> transit -> private gateway?

maya: yes. typical path: ALB -> private gateway cluster -> peering attachment -> customer VPC. ALB upstream healthy. The gateway is returning 504s because connections to the peered next-hop are timing out / RST.

liam: running quick query: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",route="private-gateway"}[1m])) by (status)` peaked at 12% 504s at 1719821050. Latency spiked to 1.8s p50 -> p95 3.4s.

kevin: rolling logs from gateway nodes: seeing `connect: connection timed out` toward 10.12.5.1 (peer ENI). Traceroute from gw-node-3 shows `* * *` at AS path hop 4 near peering appliance.

jordana: @maya can you check peering status in the cloud console and the transit appliance metrics? any CPU/conntrack exhaustion?

maya: peering attachment state is `available` but route table shows missing prefixes for the customer subnets. Transit appliance CPU normal. conntrack usage slightly elevated but not at limit (70%). Flows from gateway to peer are being dropped upstream. Could be a route propagation/regression on provider side.

liam: any config pushes in the last 30m? infra-deploy bot shows no gateway rollouts. No recent firewall rule changes in our side per audit logs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: No deploys matching gateway or peering configs in the last 2 hours.

jordana: escalated to cloud network provider support. Meanwhile we need a mitigation plan to restore traffic quickly. Options: 1) failover impacted tenants to public-egress path (temporary), 2) add static routes in our private route table pointing to secondary peer, 3) ask provider to reset peering session. Thoughts?

maya: static route add could be fast if secondary peer exists for those prefixes. I see a backup peering in another transit appliance in eu-west-1b but the route hasn't been advertised to the gateway. I can push a static route for the affected prefixes to point at the backup attachment, but need approval — this will change egress path.

sarah-cs: prioritize customer-facing fix. tenants 42 and 88 are paying enterprise with active incidents. If public-egress keeps data policy valid, prefer that for fastest recovery. Need to confirm data plane/privacy constraints for those tenants.

kevin: for tenant-42 we have a contract clause — traffic must stay on private peering. so public-egress not allowed for that one. tenant-88 OK to move.

jordana: plan: 1) move tenant-88 to public-egress route (hotfix) 2) push static route for tenant-42 to backup peering attachment (maya) 3) provider ping to reset peering session and investigate root cause.

maya: doing step 2 now. command: ```cli network route add --dest 10.240.88.0/24 --next-hop attachment-rtg-02 --priority 100 --note "incident 1719821111"``` applying to route table rt-private-gw-3

liam: I'm updating runbook and marking impacted tenants in the incident board. Pulling end-to-end traces for both tenants to verify success.

maya: static route applied on rt-private-gw-3. I can already see flows rerouted to attachment-rtg-02. Monitoring..

ops-bot: route-change: static route 10.240.88.0/24 added by maya at 1719821285.

kevin: tenant-88 pushed to public-egress (manual toggle done). Confirmed by support that errors dropped from 25% -> 1% for them.

liam: tenant-42 metrics: 504s dropped from 18% -> 2% after static route applied. p95 latency back to 400ms. Looks like baseline restored for both.

jordana: good. provider responded: they saw partial route flap due to a buggy prefix-aggregation policy on their peering appliance causing selective withdraws. They're rolling a fix and will keep the session reset under watch.

sarah-cs: replying to support tickets: "We've applied a targeted routing mitigation and are monitoring — your traffic should be restored. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

maya: I'll keep the static route for 2 hours, then coordinate with provider to restore normal propagation and remove the override. Documented steps in the runbook.

jordana: taking incident to post-incident review. TO DOs: provider RCA, add automation to failover impacted prefixes to backup attachment, add alert for route withdrawals > 10 in 5m, update runbook to include quick static-route command.

liam: filing postmortem draft and adding owner tags. Great job all.

jordana: oncall handoff: I'm handing to liam for overnight monitoring at 1719822600 — liam, you have it.

liam: taking handoff. will watch alerting and escalate if provider fix isn't stable.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rates back to baseline. Severity: P1 -> resolved (monitoring).
